children: The State Street Financial Select Sector SPDR ETF
gained 5.23% during the month, outperforming the S&P 500 (
)'s 1.40% decline, as investors assessed third-quarter earnings. However, the sector ranked seventh among the 11 S&P 500 sectors.
Seeking Alpha analyst

, Investing Group Leader for Ian's Inside Corner, said artificial intelligence (AI) was arguably the decisive factor behind much of the sector's outperformance, as sharp declines in AI-related stocks prompted capital to rotate into other areas, including financials.

Top financial sector performers of the month
Cboe Global Markets
led financial stocks, rising 21.05% during October. S&P Global
followed with a 20.20% gain, while insurance broker Arthur J. Gallagher
advanced 19.09%.
FactSet Research Systems
rose 18.09% as it was viewed as vulnerable to AI-related disruption and rebounded as sentiment toward AI-exposed businesses shifted, while Erie Indemnity
gained 17.68%.
Bezek said Cboe could benefit from increased options trading, particularly activity tied to the Cboe Volatility Index
, as heightened market uncertainty can support its business. He also pointed to a reversal in AI-related sentiment as a potential tailwind for insurance brokers and financial data providers.
Insurance brokers had faced concerns that AI agents could disrupt industry pricing models, he noted, making a slowdown in AI adoption a source of relief for the group.

Top financial sector detractors of the month
Coinbase Global
posted the steepest decline among the listed financial stocks, falling 24.17% during October. Robinhood Markets
followed with a 23.54% drop.
Charles Schwab
declined 10.49%, while Interactive Brokers Group
fell 10.38%. Invesco
rounded out the five biggest decliners, losing 8.74%.
Bezek said crypto-related stocks, equity brokerages, and asset managers were among the hardest-hit groups as risk appetite weakened in AI and cryptocurrency markets.
He also cited reported cyberattacks involving crypto exchanges, prediction markets, and financial institutions as a source of concern for companies such as Coinbase and Robinhood.

Looking Head

Despite October's gains, Bezek remained cautious on the financial stocks heading into year-end, citing a challenging macroeconomic outlook marked by weak consumer sentiment, soft housing demand, persistently high-energy prices, and the risk of an inverse wealth effect if financial markets continue to decline.
